_about: Roadmap progress. Each phase is a weighted list of items; weight is the item's share of that phase's effort, done its completion from 0 to 1. kind 'measured' means tools/progress.py computes done from the repository (or a census figure it records here); 'estimate' means a judgement, with its evidence. See docs/progress.md.

P1.item: Translation, lockstep, routes and the emulated PC (roadmap Phase 1 'Done')
P1.evidence: All 17 code files translated (89,366 instructions); instruction lockstep 0 mismatches over 5.7M states; 35 routes identical across engines; fidelity.py 1,210/1,210; housekeeping done.

Settled by scope 8 Oct 2026 (roadmap 'Settled'): the weight is cut to the work done, dropping what was left. What was left (the test pilot's 7 of 9 over a +-15% stick-scale range on 86Box) measures the pilot, not the machines. Before: Done: tools/pc_parity.py checks pictures, music and the saved roster on both against measured limits, fidelity_all.py holds the machine probe, 86Box runs are deterministic (8 Oct 2026: the harness hook in the emulation thread; repeat runs byte-identical), the closed-loop supply drop delivers on both, a closed-loop career sortie saves its roster on both (DOSBox-X's and 86Box's byte-identical, ours differing only in the mission score, which END scores the same from either machine's handover), the 86Box intro drift and pitch-bend writes are explained, and the decision to use them as the routine references is made. The 86Box adaptor sends the stick as whole game frames (the game runs at about half the frame rate there), and the supply drop, the strike-training hit and the career landing then pass on 86Box too. Open: those flights pass 7 of 9 over a +-15% range of the one estimated stick scale, so a mission with a narrow window can still miss on 86Box.

P1.item: The picture against the references, frame by frame
P1.evidence: Settled by scope 8 Oct 2026 (roadmap 'Settled'): the weight is cut to the work done, dropping what was left. What was left (one-sample DOSBox transitions whose frame follows the capture's phase) describes the capture; frame timing against a period PC moves to the 386 profile. Before: The SVGA_S3 screen-off fix removes five false black local pictures. DOSBox 0.74 source confirms fractional PIC scheduling from pixel clock/CRTC totals; local frame, line-part, retrace, status and I/O slice deadlines now use rational event times with whole-instruction ceiling boundaries. After the pc_slice_left refinement, saved independent capture intro-qlh_wi26 matches 1,329/1,332 exact pictures, with three one-sample logo images unmatched on each side and -0.000034 ms end drift. Fresh capture intro-cfku0zec matches 1,321/1,332, with 11 one-sample images unmatched on each side and +14.268 ms drift. The local 1,332-picture sequences are identical; remaining transition differences depend on reference capture phase. No multi-sample mismatch remains; exact frame parity is open. 86Box (386DX/33, MS-DOS 5.00): 85 of 86 graphics pictures exact in 6-bit DAC values, in order, the other a single sample of START's roster half drawn while its files load (pc_parity.py requires 84); its timing is a different machine's by design, so frame timing is judged against DOSBox.

What was left (an independent GOG DOSBox cargo delivery, wider generated-assignment coverage) tests reference emulators and pilots; all eight objective types have gate routes. Before: Strike and strike-return inputs have been refreshed after rational VGA slice-boundary timing and pass paired strong observers under both engines with byte-identical input, flight and result files (return clock 15029717426/hash 7b49aac1f746ffa7, result 0/status 3); both routes also pass the official world, VGAME-exit and END-debrief gates. A recomp trap-poll fix (nested guest_call returns) was needed for long observer runs; the full gate passes with it (27/27 routes identical, both locksteps 0 mismatching). Independent GOG DOSBox supply-mission generation is reproduced (exact type-3/target-24/departure-58/home-51 triple at a -275 ms seed compensating autoexec overhead); open-loop replay then diverges in flight. Air-to-air types 5-8 were re-recorded under the current timing and are gate routes (airair_type5-8), each replaying byte-identically under both engines with result 0/status 3; all eight primary objective types now have gate-replayed normal-input routes. P1.item: Rendered sound: speech and the PC speaker
P1.evidence: Scope 8 Oct 2026: matching DOSBox's OPL mixer sample for sample is dropped (the synthesis is the emulator's, the register stream the game's, and that is exact): every AdLib write of the intro matches GOG's capture in order and value (7 Oct). Speaker, shown 8 Oct 2026: the host runs PIT counter 2 clock by clock to the 8254 data sheet (src/host/speaker.c); the speaker driver's music, whose count rewrites the old renderer took at once (restarting the wave), now matches DOSBox-X's capture (tools/speaker_parity.py, intro 138 s: envelope 0.87, spectral 0.92-0.93, level 0.95; before 0.69, 0.54, 0.47), with its 736 gate changes and 440 control words identical; the radio call (counter 2 mode 0 PWM, 79-clock carrier) has its 12,924 counts identical to DOSBox-X's and renders carrier-free (realsound, default) or as the pulse train (pwm); in band it equals GOG DOSBox's count-as-level model (|r| 0.97, equal energy). Shown 9 Oct 2026 on 86Box's MS-DOS 5.00 VMs (b86_cargo_pilot.py --profile, B86_OPL / B86_SPKLOG): the takeoff call's 6,464 AdLib register-43h writes and the speaker driver's 13,046 counts are identical in order and value to this machine's, at the same rate (7,938 vs 7,936 writes a second; 15.1 counts a millisecond). Open (weight 0.23 of 5.6): an audio reference for the speech (DOSBox-X plays none of it); listening is Phase 4. Closed 9 Oct 2026: independent silent 86Box mixer capture (86box-audio.patch, speech_audio.py), MS-DOS 5.00/MOUSE.COM 6.26, speaker driver. Identical 12,924 non-silence takeoff-call counts, 855.6255 ms. In 300-3400 Hz, waveform correlation -0.991565, envelope 0.999516, zero lag and ours/reference RMS 3.16856; polarity and gain follow PIT duty (10000/79 per count) versus 86Box count-as-level (10240/256). In 100-8000 Hz correlation -0.988890, envelope 0.999437. Capture off/on has byte-identical 4,500 frame records, 1,621 AdLib writes and speaker port log. Reports repeat identically; altered count stream is rejected. This supplies the missing waveform reference; listening remains Phase 4. See tools/ref86box/build_86box.md. No runtime/default changes.

Completed 10 Oct 2026. Both engines charge the same 386DX/33 profile; all 93 probe blocks match the saved MS-DOS 5.00/MOUSE.COM 6.26 reference (AH=2Ch varies by four cycles); 5.7M instruction comparisons, repeated with code in VRAM, have zero differences including prefetch and held REP state. Paired flights have 574 identical checkpoints and stick responses. STI/SS-load shadows include zero-cycle instructions; four regressions pass. Matched entries run translated bodies under this profile. File services, EXEC and overlays are charged at the reference period disk's measured costs. The last alleged hold failure compared a default 9 MIPS capture against 86Box. Retained profile/content-aware checks and fresh full references now pass: all 21 local held pictures match, max duration difference 0.214 s (limit 0.35), drift 1.113 s (limit 2.2), final hangar 19 ms apart. Pictures, music and both roster saves pass too. Eight regression tests protect profile identity, matching and timing verdicts. Direct cycle charges in handwritten routines remain an optional performance improvement.

P3.item: Stage 1: draw lists replayed bit-exact at 320x200
P3.evidence: Whole phases rebuilt byte for byte over the 64 KB work page and the A000 display page (tools/drawlist_frame.py): 73 of 73 phases on 30M instructions of the strike flight, and every phase of 30M-instruction windows of four more routes (recon 34, Central Europe air-to-air 29, landing 38, cargo 38), with no byte copied from the original on any of them. Work-page changes replay by rule; direct display writes from uncoded graphics entries are replayed from captured byte deltas. Entry 22 (the scaled RLE sprite) is decoded and replayed, which closed the two late-flight windows that had copied bytes. The remaining work is unexercised branches (dithered fills, the sprite clip edge cases) and windows not yet captured. Live (9 Oct 2026, src/present/drawlist.c, a rule-for-rule port of drawlist_frame.py, identical output): 8 windows, 447 phases exact on the work page and display with no byte copied from the original; graphics entry 41 is a colour replace in a rectangle, now a record (M) and a rule. Left: entries that only set state (13-16, 24-26, 45, 46, 62, 65).

Model polygons re-projected from camera-space vertices and filled on a fine grid (hires_subpixel.py and src/present/hires.c; docs/presentation.md). Live --present-scale N built: all 9,845 strike logic frames equal the display at close; N=1/2/4/9 keep guest hashes unchanged. The flat-pixel guard restores the remaining 0.002-0.010% of flat blocks at N=2/4/9. Open: text, sprites, HUD and cockpit art remain scaled copies; near-clipped polygons and geometry outside the supported projection rule also remain scaled. Completion estimate unchanged pending those requirements.

P3.item: Stage 3 and 4: interpolation to 60+ fps, pacing and polish
P3.evidence: Live draw feed and interpolation built (src/present/drawfeed.c, interp.c). All 9,843 strike frame pairs exact at coarse and fine endpoints at N=1/2/4/9; guest hashes unchanged. Host presents at vsync with machine-clock t; dummy-driver 60 Hz runs measured, with original-picture switch (--present scan) and picture-age selection (--present-age interp|extrapolate). Extrapolation predicts worse than holding the old frame in 191 of 265 measured steps, so interpolation remains the presentation mode default when enabled. See docs/presentation.md for cost and frame intervals. Open: HUD/text source at 4K, real-display refresh/motion/4K checks and polish. Completion estimate unchanged pending those requirements.
